title: Yoneda Ext product agrees with derived-category composition
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and define $\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal A}(M,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],N[0][i])$ as in [def-pc-ext]. For objects $L,M,N$ and classes $a\in\operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathcal A}(M,N)$ and $b\in\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal A}(L,M)$, the Yoneda product $a\circ b\in\operatorname{Ext}^{i+j}_{\mathcal A}(L,N)$ is the derived-category composite obtained by shifting $a$ by $j$ and composing it with $b$, using the standard shift identification. In degree zero this is ordinary composition, and composing with a degree-zero morphism $u:L\to M$ or $\varphi:N\to N'$ gives respectively $a\circ u$ or $\varphi[i]\circ a$.
